description:
Trim comments and rustdoc in the crates and tools this epic touched to the non-obvious-only standard.

## Background

AGENTS.md (correctness and test policy) now states that comments and rustdoc carry only what the code leaves non-obvious: the contract, an invariant, the reason behind a choice, or a pointer to evidence, in the shortest form that conveys it, with history kept in git and jit and a module orientation of at most one short paragraph. Files touched since the epic began (`git diff --name-only bd186992^ HEAD -- crates dev/tools`) run to 63% comment lines in `crates/gf2-core/src/field/traits.rs`, 46% in `crates/gf2-core/src/gf2m/wide.rs` and 37% in the new `crates/gf2-core/src/gf2m/byte_table.rs`, and eleven files under `crates/` narrate task, story or session history inside rustdoc.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every Rust file in the set `git diff --name-only bd186992^ HEAD -- crates dev/tools` meets the AGENTS.md comment rule: no comment restates the adjacent code, no rustdoc narrates commit, task, story or session history, and each module-level doc is at most one short orientation paragraph plus the contract statements the public API needs.
- [hard] REQ-02: Across `crates/` and `dev/tools/`, `grep -rnE '^\s*//[/!].*(Task [0-9]|story `|session [0-9]|nee `|Historically)'` returns no line.
- [hard] REQ-03: Public API rustdoc still states purpose, panics, safety conditions and non-obvious complexity; `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` builds without warnings and `./scripts/cargo-ci.sh` passes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Behaviour is untouched: the change contains only comment, rustdoc and whitespace edits, verified with `git diff --ignore-all-space --stat` and a review of every hunk.
- [hard] REQ-05: The commit message or a linked record reports the comment-line share of each edited file before and after.

## Notes

Comment-only change; no timed runs. Run after the epic's remaining code work so trimmed files are not rewritten by later tasks.
title: Trim comments and rustdoc in epic-touched files to the non-obvious-only standard
